messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: sev=high network fabric anomalies detected impacting distributed serving clusters (us-west-2). Symptoms: sporadic IB packet reordering, elevated retransmits, node flaps leading to container restarts and CUDA OOMs. Auto-diagnostics running. Acknowledge to claim.

oncall-amy: ack. pulling alerts and paging @sre-mike and @infra-sara.

sre-mike: looking at cluster telemetry. I'm seeing a pattern: brief bursts of packet reordering on lanes attached to serve-uw2-04/06, followed by pod evictions and gpu driver messages: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:05:12Z] mlx5_core: port 1 link flapping detected
[2026-03-15T14:05:15Z] nvidia-driver: gpu0: cuModuleLoadDataEx -> cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[2026-03-15T14:05:16Z] kubelet: Pod serving-worker-xyz restarted (OOMKilled)
```

infra-sara: we just deployed a ToR ingress firmware at 13:58Z to address QoS scheduling. I see ECN counters increased and subsequent retransmit spikes. also some SFP link errors on the uplink to spine-3. opening ticket with colo.

oncall-amy: immediate actions: 1) cordon serve-uw2-04 & serve-uw2-06, 2) enable cross-region routing to us-west-1 for critical routes, 3) spin up reserved spare pool and shift canary traffic. Starting cordon now.

sre-mike: cordon/drain commands running: `kubectl cordon serve-uw2-04 && kubectl drain serve-uw2-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — note: some long-lived KV-cache writes in-memory; draining will evict in-flight inferences which may trigger OOM. capture caches first if reachable.

ops-bot: autoscaler: increased dedicated-spares-west by +8 nodes to maintain QPS.

pm-lina: customer impact: error rate for /v1/chat in us-west-2 jumped from 0.1% to 4.5% in the last 8m; 95p latency for gen routes rose to 5.2s. Several paid customers reported timeouts. Drafting customer blurb.

cs-omar: creating CS incident with initial impact list. tagging support engineers.

infra-sara: running `ibv_devinfo` and `ethtool` — ports show rx_crc_errors and rx_no_buffer high on the affected NICs. suspecting either MTU mismatch or firmware regression causing ECN marking storms. I can attempt ToR rollback; will coordinate with colo.

sre-mike: collecting runtime logs and heap traces: `journalctl -u serving-runtime` shows repeated cudaMalloc failures while the process attempts to recover from partial KV cache reloads. saving logs to /var/incidents/2247001234/logs.tgz.

oncall-amy: routing update pushed: traffic weight for us-west-2 reduced to 10% for non-critical routes; critical tenants moved to us-west-1 fallback. Also allowed model fallback to q8_0_single_node for latency-sensitive endpoints - note this will change output characteristics.

incident-bot: AUTO: model-fallback enabled: q8_0_single_node for routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat in us-west-2.

pm-lina: customer note draft: "We're investigating increased errors in us-west-2 due to a networking issue. We've shifted critical traffic to an alternate region and enabled fallback model variants to preserve availability. We'll provide updates within 30 minutes."

cs-omar: sent to impacted customers, included mitigation and workaround.

infra-sara: colo: confirmed partial rollback of ToR firmware at 14:17Z. SFP replacement scheduled for 14:30Z on uplink to spine-3. link flaps decreased on ToR-B but serve-uw2-06 still shows elevated retransmit and reorder.

sre-mike: after moving traffic and draining nodes, success-rate for affected routes rose from ~60% to ~95% in 6m. still seeing isolated CrashLoopBackOff on two pods that were mid-inference — stack shows cuda OOM on resume: 
```
serving-runtime[pid=2123]: cudaMalloc(1.5G) failed: out of memory
stacktrace: runtime/infer.c:487
```

oncall-amy: any quick mitigations for preventing immediate OOM kills during these flaps?

sre-mike: temp mitigation: set vm.overcommit_memory=1 and reduce oom_kill_allocating_task where possible on those nodes, and temporarily increase per-pod gpu memory limits to avoid oversubscription during reschedule. doing sysctl tweak now. not recommended long-term.

infra-sara: colo reports SFP swapped and optics healthy now. I'm continuing to watch ECN/retransmit counters. opening ticket 987612 with vendor for firmware regression analysis.

pm-lina: impact summary for RCA notes: scope: partial us-west-2 cluster; customers impacted: ~8 enterprise tenants + percentage of self-serve traffic; root cause hypothesis: ToR firmware QoS/ECN change -> increased ECN marks + MTU/flow mismatch -> IB packet reordering & retransmits -> runtime stalls and pod restarts causing CUDA OOMs during reschedule. Mitigations: node cordon/drain, ToR rollback, SFP replacement, cross-region reroute, enable quantized single-node fallbacks, scale spare pool.

cs-omar: logged affected customers and attached mitigation steps into ticket RED-2247.

oncall-amy: handoff plan: I will hand over to @sre-mike in 20m to continue RCA and artifact collection. I'll paste a short summary for the oncall log.

sre-mike: accepting handoff. I'll gather pcap from colo, runtime memprofiles, kube evictions timeline, and run long-run soak on repaired nodes before returning them to pool.

oncall-amy: handoff summary to paste: "Network fabric instability in us-west-2 after ToR firmware change caused ECN surge and packet reordering leading to retransmits, node flaps, and container restart OOMs. Immediate actions: cordon/drain affected nodes, rollback ToR firmware, swap SFP, reroute traffic to us-west-1, enable q8 fallback, scale spares. Customer comms sent. Next steps: gather switch pcaps, vendor firmware RCA, analyze container memory pressure during reschedule, and add pre-deploy network compatibility checks."

ops-bot: Reminder: oncall shift ends for @oncall-amy in 18m.

pm-lina: I'll own customer communications and timeline. estimate time to verify full restoration: 1-3 hours pending vendor analysis and soak.

infra-sara: requested switch pcap for ports attached to serve-uw2-04/06/09; colo provided initial capture, sending to /var/incidents/2247001234/pcaps.

sre-mike: saving runtime artifacts and KV-cache snapshots to /var/incidents/2247001234/. I'll create RCA doc and schedule postmortem.

oncall-amy: handing off to @sre-mike at 14:26Z. Phone available for escalation. thanks team. :thumbsup: 

sre-mike: acknowledged. continuing RCA. tagging @pm-lina for postmortem scheduling.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied; user-visible error rate reduced. Next update in 30 minutes or on status change.

cs-omar: confirming customers notified; support ticket updated with workarounds for routing adjustments.

pm-lina: post-incident actions: 1) Add pre-deploy ECN/MTU verification to network rollout checklist, 2) Validate runtime behavior on transient IB reorders, 3) Add automated regional reroute tests to chaos harness, 4) Document KV-cache persistence best-practices for safe drains.

infra-sara: monitoring for 45m. no new link flaps after ToR rollback and SFP swap.

oncall-amy: closing pager handoff. current success rate 99.2% for serving routes. keep monitoring windows.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: fabric stable; affected nodes quarantined for soak; RCA in progress. Postmortem scheduled.
